newsitem.title: USA: Violent storms hit Southeast Michigan, Detroit.
newsitem.headline: Violent storms hit Southeast Michigan, Detroit.

text.p: Wayne County and Detroit officials declared a state of emergency Wednesday night after surveying massive damage left by thunderstorms and tornadoes that ripped apart homes and caused at least five deaths.

Police confirmed four people in Grosse Pointe Farms were killed -- three children and an adult -- when the picnic shelter they were under was picked up and swept into Lake St. Clair by a tornado or high winds.
A woman was killed and another person was missing after a tornado hit a mobile home park in Springfield Township, about 50 miles northwest of Detroit.
Throughout the three-country Detroit area, police closed off streets and utility crews worked into the night to restore power to an estimated 200,000 homes.

Trying to head off looters, Detroit Police called in extra officers. Wayne County Sheriff Robert Ficano said the jail was locked down to free extra officers. Despite the efforts, there were some reports of looting from damaged stores.

Swirling with winds of 60 to 100 mph, the storms, including at least 10 tornadoes, smashed into the area shortly before evening rush hour. They triggered alarms, flipped cars, downed power lines and dumped up to four inches of rain, prompting flash flood warnings.

Two of the areas hardest hit were the Detroit communities of Highland Park and Hamtramck. Jeseca Woodard, 17, told Reuters she was upstairs in her Highland Park home when the lights starting blinking and high winds began blowing in the windows.
"I closed my eyes because I didn't want to get glass in them and when I opened my eyes, I looked up and I could see the sky," she said.
After realizing the roof had been blown off, Woodard, who was not injured, said she ran into the basement to wait out the storm with her mother.
"The attic was gone and everything," she said.
Other witnesses told stories of odd devestation, including a garage that was lifted from its foundation, leaving the car inside untouched.
The storm passed quickly. By 7 p.m., most of the violent weather had moved east toward Canada and the sun was shining in the western parts of the Detroit metro area.
